title: Family Homes for Rent in Phuket Under ฿60,000 a Month
excerpt: We list 104 houses and villas with three or more bedrooms for ฿60,000 a month or less, at a median of ฿45,000. Where they are, what you get, and what families should ask.
author: Islander Home Team
content:
Families moving to Phuket typically need three bedrooms, a garden and a quiet street, ideally within easy reach of a school. Finding a home that meets these needs is easier, and often more affordable, than many people expect, provided you look beyond the beach areas.

As of early November 2026 we list 267 houses, villas and townhouses for rent with three or more bedrooms. 104 of them cost ฿60,000 a month or less. The figures below cover those 104 properties.

The numbers

  • Median rent: ฿45,000 a month
  • Cheapest: ฿25,000 a month
  • Bedrooms: 86 have three bedrooms and 18 have four
  • Type: 88 houses, 8 townhouses and 8 villas
  • Gated or with 24-hour security: 43 of the 104
  • Pet-friendly: 14 say pets are welcome
  • Private pool: 6

Koh Kaew and Thalang account for almost two-thirds of the properties. Sixty-seven of the 104 are located in these two areas, mostly in gated estates such as Supalai Bella, Habitia, Saransiri, Supalai Primo and Anasiri. Koh Kaew is close to BISP, while Thalang is close to UWC Thailand and Robinson Thalang.

A few examples from the current list

  • A renovated three-bedroom house in Si Sunthon, Thalang: ฿30,000 a month
  • A three-bedroom family house at Supalai Bella, Koh Kaew: ฿35,000 a month
  • A three-bedroom house at Pruksa Ville Kathu-Samkong: ฿40,000 a month
  • A house two minutes from BISP at Habitia, Koh Kaew: ฿45,000 a month
  • A four-bedroom pool villa with a 13-metre pool, Thalang: ฿50,000 a month
  • A four-bedroom house beside BISP at Saransiri: ฿60,000 a month

What families should ask

  • The school run. Drive the route during school hours before signing a lease. A journey that takes ten minutes on a map can take thirty in the morning.
  • Estate facilities. Many estates offer shared pools, playgrounds or gyms. Check whether these facilities are included and available to tenants.
  • Furniture. Request an inventory and ask whether the owner is willing to add or remove items such as beds and desks.
  • Pets. If you have a dog, get permission in writing. The term "small pets" can mean different things to different owners.

If you are looking for a home near a particular school, see renting near the international schools. Before signing a lease, read before you sign a lease in Phuket.
